cookingFundamentalsGuide.title: The Basics: A Really Useful Cookbook
cookingFundamentalsGuide.author: Anthony Telford
cookingFundamentalsGuide.description: Master essential cooking techniques and build your foundation for culinary success
cookingFundamentalsGuide.introduction: Every good cook starts with mastering fundamental techniques. These techniques form the foundation for all other cooking methods and develop muscle memory, timing skills, and an intuitive understanding of how food behaves.

basicCookingMethods.name: Boiling

technique.step4: Remove when done (test with fork or taste)

basicCookingMethods.timing: Varies by ingredient (pasta 8-12 min, potatoes 15-20 min, eggs 8-10 min)
tips: Use enough water to prevent temperature drop when food is added
Add salt to water (seasons food, raises boiling point slightly)
Don't overcrowd pot (prevents temperature drop)
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking
Cover lid only for water heating; remove lid while cooking to prevent boil-over

basicCookingMethods.name: Steaming
basicCookingMethods.description: Cooking food using steam (212°F / 100°C) without direct contact with water
basicCookingMethods.equipment: Steamer basket, bamboo steamer, or colander over water

technique.step1: Add water to bottom of pot (doesn't touch steamer rack)

basicCookingMethods.timing: Varies: vegetables 5-10 min, fish 8-15 min, dumplings 10-15 min
tips: Water shouldn't touch food (only steam cooks)
Refill water during steaming (doesn't boil away)
Keep steam basket covered (loses heat if opened frequently)
Arrange food in single layer (ensures even cooking)

basicCookingMethods.name: Simmering
basicCookingMethods.description: Cooking food in liquid at 180-200°F (82-93°C) with gentle bubbles

technique.step4: Cover partially or fully as recipe indicates
technique.step5: Simmer for required time (minutes to hours)

basicCookingMethods.timing: Minutes to hours depending on ingredients and tenderness goal
tips: Gentle heat prevents tough meat from becoming mushy on outside/raw inside
Partially covering allows some evaporation (concentrates flavors)
Fully covering retains more liquid
Occasional stirring prevents sticking and ensures even cooking
Adding too much liquid at start - it will reduce over time
advantages: Allows time for spices/seasonings to infuse

basicCookingMethods.name: Sautéing
basicCookingMethods.description: Cooking food quickly in a small amount of hot fat
basicCookingMethods.equipment: Wide, shallow pan (allows moisture to evaporate)

technique.step3: Heat fat until shimmering (just before smoking)
technique.step5: Don't move food - let it brown (2-3 minutes)

basicCookingMethods.timing: Fast - vegetables 5-10 minutes, meat depends on thickness
tips: Pat food dry before sautéing (moisture prevents browning)
Don't overcrowd pan (causes steaming instead of browning)
Let food rest in pan before stirring (browning takes time)
Use medium-high heat (high causes burning, medium prevents browning)
Add vegetables in order of cooking time (hard vegetables first)
fatSelection: Olive oil: good flavor, smoke point 375-400°F
Vegetable oil: neutral, high smoke point 450°F
Combination: balance flavor and heat tolerance
disadvantages: High heat can burn if not careful

basicCookingMethods.name: Pan-Frying / Shallow Frying
basicCookingMethods.description: Cooking food in ½ to 1 inch of hot fat

technique.step1: Heat ½-1 inch fat in shallow pan
technique.step2: Test readiness (drop of batter sizzles immediately)
technique.step4: Cook 3-5 minutes per side until golden

tips: Use thermometer (340-350°F is ideal range)
Don't move food too soon (outer surface needs to brown and crisp)
Keep fat at consistent temperature (too hot burns, too cool produces greasy food)
Drain on paper towels to remove excess oil

basicCookingMethods.name: Deep Frying
basicCookingMethods.description: Submerging food in hot fat (completely submerged)

technique.step1: Heat 2-3 inches fat to proper temperature
technique.step3: Carefully place food in hot fat

safetyTips: Keep baking soda nearby (in case of fire - never use water)
Dry food completely before frying (water causes splattering)
Add food slowly (hot oil can bubble over)
Use long tongs or slotted spoon (protects hands)
temperatureManagement: Too hot (above 375°F): burnt outside, raw inside
Just right (350°F): crispy outside, cooked inside

basicCookingMethods.name: Roasting
basicCookingMethods.description: Cooking food in oven with dry heat, often with some fat

technique.step3: Add small amount of fat (oil, butter, cooking spray)
technique.step6: Check doneness by temperature or texture

basicCookingMethods.timing: Depends on size: vegetables 20-30 min, chicken 1.5 hours
tips: Use high-sided roasting pan (catches drippings for gravy)
Place vegetables cut-side down (flat surface browns better)
Don't crowd pan (prevents steaming)
Stir vegetables halfway through
Meat should rest 5-10 minutes after roasting
advantages: Can cook whole meals in one pan

basicCookingMethods.name: Baking
basicCookingMethods.description: Cooking food in enclosed oven with dry heat

technique.step2: Prepare food (shape dough, arrange in dish)
technique.step3: Place in oven at specified temperature
technique.step5: Check doneness (visual cues, temperature, or touch)

criticalFactors: Not opening oven door frequently (temperature drops)

basicCookingMethods.name: Grilling
basicCookingMethods.description: Cooking food over direct heat (charcoal or gas flames)

technique.step5: Don't move food until grill marks form (3-4 minutes)

basicCookingMethods.timing: Varies: steaks 4-6 min per side, vegetables 5-8 min
tips: Create hot and cool zones (move food to cool side if charring too fast)
Use indirect heat for thick cuts (move to side away from flames)
Close lid to finish thick items (acts like oven)
Meat should rest 5 minutes after grilling

basicCookingMethods.name: Braising
basicCookingMethods.description: Browning food, then slow cooking in liquid

technique.step2: Brown food on all sides (develops flavor)
technique.step7: Cover and cook low and slow (oven or stovetop)

basicCookingMethods.timing: 1-3+ hours depending on meat size and toughness
tips: Use Dutch oven (heats evenly, retains heat)
Brown food before braising (Maillard reaction adds flavor)
Don't overcrowd pot (meat won't brown properly)
Keep liquid level consistent (top up if needed)
advantages: Can be made ahead (improves with time)
disadvantages: Produces large quantities (good for batch cooking)

essentialSkills.name: Mise en Place (Everything in Its Place)
essentialSkills.description: Preparing and organizing all ingredients before cooking begins
process: Prep all ingredients (wash, chop, mince, etc.)
Arrange ingredients in order of use
benefits: Allows you to focus on cooking technique

essentialSkills.name: Testing for Doneness
essentialSkills.description: Determining when food is properly cooked

methods.tips: Insert into thickest part, away from bone

methods.indicators: Color change, steam, flaking (fish), golden brown (baked)

methods.description: Compare firmness to palm: rare (soft), medium (firm), done (very firm)
Sample small piece; should be tender but not mushy

essentialSkills.importance: Overcooking dries out food; undercooking can pose food safety risks

essentialSkills.name: Seasoning
essentialSkills.description: Building flavor with salt, acid, and spices

principles.role: Enhances all flavors; use throughout cooking, not just at end
Brightens flavors; adds liveliness to dishes
principles.timing: Add at end (cooking diminishes acid taste)

principles.blooming: Toast spices in oil/fat to release flavors
principles.fresh_vs_dried: Fresh herbs at end, dried early in cooking

essentialSkills.layeringFlavors: Add different seasonings throughout cooking for depth

essentialSkills.name: Temperature Control
essentialSkills.description: Managing heat for proper cooking results
management: Adjust heat to maintain desired temperature
Understand your specific stove (some run hot/cold)

commonMistakes.result: Food sticks, browns unevenly, takes longer
commonMistakes.solution: Preheat pan until it's hot; test by sprinkling water (should bead and roll)

commonMistakes.mistake: Moving food too soon while browning
commonMistakes.result: Food doesn't brown, sticks to pan
commonMistakes.solution: Let food sit 3-5 minutes before stirring (browning takes time)

commonMistakes.result: Food steams instead of browns; temperature drops
commonMistakes.solution: Use larger pan or work in batches (give food space)

commonMistakes.result: Bland food; can't taste salt when added at end
commonMistakes.solution: Taste and season throughout cooking (layer flavors)
Use thermometer; remove at target temperature; let rest

commonMistakes.mistake: Not letting meat rest after cooking
commonMistakes.result: Juices run out onto plate, meat is dry
commonMistakes.solution: Rest 5-10 minutes after cooking (allows juices to redistribute)
Check doneness with window or at end; avoid opening mid-bake
